record.original_question: Is the Bergman metric complete on bounded pseudoconvex domains whose boundary regularity is less than C^1?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2.1 Is B complete on bounded pseudoconvex domains with less than C 1 boundary? -J. McNeal, mcneal@math.princeton.edu

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded pseudoconvex domain. The Bergman kernel $K_\Omega(z,w)$ of $\Omega$ is the reproducing kernel of the Hilbert space $A^2(\Omega)$ of square-integrable holomorphic functions on $\Omega$. The Bergman metric is the Kähler metric on $\Omega$ with coefficients
$$g_{i\bar j}(z) = \frac{\partial^2}{\partial z_i\, \partial \bar z_j} \log K_\Omega(z,z).$$
The domain $\Omega$ is said to be Bergman complete if it is a complete metric space with respect to the distance induced by the Bergman metric.

Assume that the boundary $\partial\Omega$ has regularity strictly less than $C^1$ (for example, only continuous, Hölder, or otherwise non-$C^1$). 

Question: Is every bounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ whose boundary has less than $C^1$ regularity Bergman complete? If not, determine the minimal boundary regularity assumptions under which Bergman completeness holds.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: B.-Y. Chen and Herbort showed that bounded hyperconvex domains are Bergman complete, and Demailly proved that bounded pseudoconvex domains with Lipschitz boundary are hyperconvex, hence Bergman complete. Thus the question is settled affirmatively for Lipschitz boundaries, but the fully general case of arbitrary less-than-$C^1$ (e.g., merely continuous or non-Lipschitz) boundaries does not appear to be completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: Hyperconvexity and Bergman completeness (Błocki–Pflug)
status_evidence.snippet: Hyperconvex bounded domains are Bergman complete; combined with Demailly's result that Lipschitz pseudoconvex domains are hyperconvex.
status_evidence.claim: Lipschitz bounded pseudoconvex domains are Bergman complete.

status_evidence.title: Completeness of the Bergman metric on non-smooth pseudoconvex domains
status_evidence.snippet: Any bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary is complete with respect to the Bergman metric.
status_evidence.claim: Partial affirmative answer for Lipschitz boundaries.
